newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan police arrest 10 leftists, says party.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan police arrest 10 leftists, says party.

text.p: Moroccan police have arrested 10 members of a leftist opposition party campaigning for a boycott of a referendum on constitutional reforms, a party spokesman said on Friday.

"Ten militants of the Avant-Garde Democratic and Socialist Party (PADS), including two lawyers, were arrested by security forces in Rabat and in the eastern city of Oujda, while distributing the party's statement on the referendum," the spokesman said.
The PADS, a legal opposition group, earlier issued a statement inviting Moroccans to boycott the referendum, being held on Friday.
An Interior Ministry official said he was not aware of the arrests.

The party named those held on Thursday as Mohamed Tarek, Ali Amar, Abdeslam Chaouch and his wife Ferdaous Tamsouri, Boudribila Abdelwahed, Rachid Chokhman, Mohamed Salhi, Abdelkader Salhi, Abdallah Bouamoud, Hussein Hadoudi.
More than 12 million people were expected to vote on Friday in a referendum on constitutional reforms that include splitting the existing 333-seat parliament into two chambers.
King Hassan, who has called for a 'yes' vote, said the amendments would strengthen regional representation and reinforce the Moroccan democratic experience.
In its statement on the constitutional reforms, the PADS said "the new amendment aims in reality at the reproduction of past failed political experiences and setting up a 'facade of democracy'."

Earlier this week, the independent Moroccan Human Rights Association said 11 PADS militants were also arrested over the last six days in Sale, the twin city of Rabat, and in the eastern town of Berkan for the same reasons.
It added that they were released later with no explanation.
